audit_findings.title: Potential NCI leakage into parent-common owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $63.841 million of 2025 NCI distributions, equal to 101.3% of the $63.0 million OE anchor; exact leakage unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated MP GOM cash flows and bridge cash may enter OE attributable to parent common shareholders without removing the 20% NCI claim, while the share denominator contains only parent shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Murphy reports 100 % of the sales volume, revenues, costs, assets and liabilities including the 20 % noncontrolling interest in MP GOM in accordance with accounting for noncontrolling interest as prescribed by Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 810-10-45, “Consolidations”.
audit_findings.explanation: Consolidation of MP GOM is demonstrated, but leakage in the OE calculation is not yet demonstrated because the component-level reconciliation was not supplied. The potential is material: one year's NCI distributions exceeded the entire anchor, so an attributable-perimeter correction could substantially reduce or eliminate modeled operating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile operating cash flow, noncash adjustments, capital expenditures, ARO settlements and cash to Murphy-attributable amounts; identify any NCI distributions already deducted and rerun all scenarios only after eliminating duplication or leakage.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 OE does not contain the interest cost of the net 2026 borrowing increase
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed recurring pre-tax net interest increase of approximately $12.352 million annually before fee amortization: $32.500 million on the new notes less $4.635 million, $9.473 million and $6.040 million on redeemed notes and repaid RCF debt; 19.6% of the $63.0 million anchor and approximately $173.5 million or $1.17/share of base PV if applied proportionally
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model and debt principal is not deducted, post-transaction interest expense must reduce anchor OE and every projected cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: In particular, the Company closed a public offering of $ 500.0 million aggregate principal amount of its 2034 Notes, used the proceeds to redeem an aggregate $ 227.5 million of its outstanding 2027 Notes and 2028 Notes, repaid $ 100.0 million that was outstanding on the previous RCF, as of December 31, 2025, and expects to use the remaining proceeds to cover transaction-related fees and expenses and for general corporate purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch: FY2025 could not include the recurring cost of debt issued in January 2026. The filed coupon and redeemed-debt amounts establish a potentially material run-rate increase, although the final after-tax effect and fee amortization require a normalized calculation.
audit_findings.action: Construct post-refinancing run-rate interest using the June 2026 debt structure, remove interest on redeemed debt and the repaid RCF, add recurring fee amortization and applicable cash-tax effects, then rerun the valuation from normalized OE.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may be stale against the 2026 capital program
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest 2026 capital guidance is $1.500-$1.600 billion excluding NCI, $343-$443 million above 2025 capital expenditures excluding acquisitions and NCI of $1.157 billion, or 5.4x-7.0x the $63.0 million anchor; attributable OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A discrete change in operating cash generation or attributable capital spending changes the starting OE before scenario growth is applied.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s capital expenditure spend for 2026 is expected to be between $1,200 million and $1,300 million, excluding NCI.
audit_findings.explanation: Use of FY2025 as the latest-actual anchor is demonstrably stale relative to the available first-half 2026 filing, and updated capital guidance is even higher than the amount cited by the audit. Materiality is established by the spending increase relative to the thin anchor. Direction remains mixed because first-half 2026 also benefited from higher oil prices and lower lease operating costs, producing $151.4 million of reported FCF before shareholder and financing adjustments.
audit_findings.action: Calculate trailing-twelve-month and year-to-date 2026 parent-attributable OE under the identical valuation rules, normalize commodity prices and unusual workover or exploration items, incorporate the revised $1.500-$1.600 billion capital program, and rerun from any supported step-change.

audit_findings.title: Large decommissioning claims may not be captured by a one-year OE run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,040.586 million ARO at June 30, 2026, equal to 76.0% of the $1.369 billion base equity value; $70.829 million settled in 2025 and $59.231 million classified current at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Actual abandonment payments reduce OE, while any future decommissioning cash not represented in projected OE or terminal value is an omitted claim on common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The ARO liabilities recognized by the Company are related to the estimated costs to dismantle and abandon its producing oil and natural gas properties and related equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and its scale are demonstrated, but omission is not: operating cash flow may already include actual settlements, and the supplied record does not show the OE treatment. A one-year settlement amount nevertheless cannot validate the life-of-field burden, whose recorded balance is large relative to the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Trace 2025 and 2026 ARO cash settlements through operating cash flow and OE, confirm the treatment of accretion and settlement gains or losses, obtain the attributable undiscounted abandonment schedule by field, and rerun explicit and terminal cash flows with that schedule.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be surplus distributable cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $483.875 million bridge addition, equal to $3.27/share and 35.3% of the $1.369 billion base equity value; $160.2 million was held outside the U.S. and the June 2026 net working-capital liability was $175.5 million; non-surplus amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Only unrestricted parent-attributable cash exceeding operating, working-capital, capital-program, NCI and tax requirements belongs in the equity bridge without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company will primarily fund its capital program in 2026 using operating cash flow and available cash.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the complete June cash balance is demonstrated, but the amount that is genuinely surplus is unresolved. The filing states that available cash funds the capital program and identifies foreign balances and a working-capital deficit. Because cash supplies more than one-third of base equity value, even a partial restriction could materially change value.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 2026 cash waterfall separating restricted or NCI-owned cash, minimum operating liquidity, working-capital needs, committed near-term capital, dividends, foreign withholding or repatriation costs and genuinely distributable parent cash; rerun the bridge with only the supported surplus.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth requires economic reserve replacement, not merely production spending
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed base terminal value of approximately $439.8 million, equal to 49.7% of the $885.0 million operating PV, $2.98/share and 32.1% of the $1.369 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Reserve-replacement economics determine whether OE can persist and grow at the 2.5% terminal rate after development, exploration, lease, infrastructure and abandonment spending.
audit_findings.evidence: Murphy continually depletes its oil and natural gas reserves as production occurs.
audit_findings.explanation: No demonstrated error establishes that economic replacement is inadequate: the filing reports 101% proved-reserve replacement in 2025. That volume statistic does not establish the after-capital return required for perpetual OE growth. Because nearly half of operating value comes from the terminal calculation, the unsupported economic-replacement assumption is presently material rather than merely a monitoring item.
audit_findings.action: Build an attributable reserve-replacement test using normalized commodity prices, reserve additions excluding revisions and acquisitions, development and exploration spending including failures, lease and infrastructure commitments, and abandonment costs; rerun terminal value under the economically supported growth rate.
